Threat.value: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
Remembering what happened during the frightening event is just like looking at photographs of it in my mind.

Negative Appraisals.value: I can't trust that I will do the right thing
I have failed in my most important role in life
I was betrayed by someone I trusted

issues.item: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: For trauma type 'physical abuse by romantic partner', the appraisal 'I feel guilty for surviving when others did not' is clinically hard to reconcile because this trauma does not ordinarily involve other deaths or a mass-casualty context. The rest of the profile centers on partner violence, hypervigilance, and fragmented visual recall, so this item introduces a markedly different trauma scenario without support elsewhere in the selected items.

'Car sounds' is difficult to connect clinically to the rest of this profile for physical abuse by a romantic partner. The other trigger items and all threat, memory, and appraisal items center on interpersonal trauma, bodily alarm, betrayal, and fragmented terror-based recall. A car-sound trigger suggests a different trauma context unless there is supporting material elsewhere, so this item is the main coherence concern.

vignette: Rohan's eyes would often glaze over when he tried to recall that fateful night three years ago. He and his wife, Nalini, had been arguing in their living room, the tension between them palpable. The sound of raised voices, incomprehensible chatter, still echoed in his mind like a cacophony. Rohan remembered feeling a surge of adrenaline as he saw Nalini's face contort with rage, her eyes flashing like knives. She had never hit him before, but that night was different. He recalled the sensation of her palm connecting with his cheekbone, the shock and pain radiating through his face. In the months following the incident, Rohan began to notice changes in himself. Whenever he felt physically unwell, even with something as minor as a cold, he would be transported back to that night. The memories came flooding back – the terror, the helplessness, the feeling of being trapped. It was as if his body had developed a hair-trigger response to any perceived threat. He couldn't shake off the sense that danger lurked around every corner, waiting to pounce. At work, Rohan found himself struggling to concentrate on designs and blueprints. As an architect, he needed to be precise and focused, but his mind kept wandering back to the night of the incident. The sound of colleagues chatting in the background would sometimes morph into incomprehensible chatter, sending a shiver down his spine. He started avoiding meetings and social gatherings, unable to bear the thought of being in crowded spaces where he might feel trapped or vulnerable. The smell of alcohol also triggered Rohan's memories. Nalini had been drinking that night, and the pungent aroma still lingered in his nostrils like a ghostly presence. He would avoid bars and restaurants, afraid of being confronted with the same scent that transported him back to the traumatic event. Rohan's sleep patterns suffered as well. He found himself lying awake at night, alert and vigilant, waiting for... something. It was as if his body had learned to react before his mind could process the threat. The startle response became second nature – a sudden noise would make him jump, his heart racing like a jackrabbit. Despite his best efforts, memories of that night persisted. They came in snapshots, frozen moments in time that Rohan couldn't shake off. He remembered Nalini's face twisted with rage, her eyes flashing with anger. The images were seared into his mind like photographs, each one evoking the same terror he felt on that fateful night. Rohan began to doubt himself, wondering if he had somehow contributed to the incident. Had he failed as a husband? As a partner? He couldn't shake off the feeling of having let Nalini down, of being inadequate in some fundamental way. The sense of betrayal lingered, like an open wound that refused to heal. As time passed, Rohan's relationships began to suffer. His friends and family noticed a change in him – he was withdrawn, distant, and irritable. His work suffered as well; his designs lacked the flair and creativity they once had. It was as if Rohan had lost himself in the aftermath of that traumatic night. It wasn't until Nalini's recent threats to leave him that Rohan realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, trapped in a cycle of fear and self-doubt. With a sense of trepidation, he made an appointment with a therapist, hoping to untangle the web of emotions that had ensnared him for so long.
